nodes.label: Dormant Security Assurance Bundle Configuration
nodes.rationale: All Security Assurance runtime rows are installed disabled so deployment owners explicitly activate qualified capabilities.

nodes.label: Security Assurance Is an Independent Companion Product
nodes.source_location: # Security Assurance is an independent companion product
nodes.rationale: Preserve an independently useful security product while keeping Engineering Control Plane governance provider-neutral.

nodes.label: Security Verdicts Do Not Own Mission Approval
nodes.source_location: # Security Verdicts do not own Mission approval
nodes.rationale: The Control Plane must remain the sole authority over Mission approval, rework, and operational indeterminacy.

nodes.label: Codex Security Is a Reference, Not a Required Runtime
nodes.source_location: # Codex Security is a reference, not a required runtime
nodes.rationale: DSH owns its contracts and avoids copying private Codex implementation or requiring a Codex-specific runtime.

nodes.label: Security Claims Are Scope and Coverage Bound
nodes.source_location: # Security claims are scope- and coverage-bound
nodes.rationale: Missing required coverage must produce an indeterminate verdict; successful execution or zero findings cannot imply satisfaction.

nodes.label: One Assessment Engine Serves Both Entry Points
nodes.source_location: # One Assessment Engine serves both entry points
nodes.rationale: Standalone and Control Plane entry points must preserve one evidence and verdict meaning for equivalent frozen inputs.

nodes.label: Security Assessments Bind an Immutable Subject
nodes.source_location: # Security Assessments bind an immutable Subject
nodes.rationale: Exact identities and digests prevent later workspace mutation from changing what an Assessment evaluated.

nodes.label: Host Policy and a Deterministic Evaluator Own Verdict Semantics
nodes.source_location: # Host Policy and a deterministic evaluator own Verdict semantics
nodes.rationale: Analyzers contribute evidence, findings, and coverage, while only frozen policy and deterministic evaluation derive the verdict.

nodes.label: Security Verdicts Are Tristate and Fail Closed
nodes.source_location: # Security Verdicts are tristate and fail closed
nodes.rationale: Satisfied requires complete eligible coverage and no blocking finding; proven violations fail, and uncertainty remains indeterminate.

nodes.label: Evidence Storage Does Not Modify the Assessment Subject
nodes.source_location: # Evidence storage does not modify the Assessment Subject
nodes.rationale: Canonical evidence remains plugin-owned so assessment activity cannot mutate or trust target-controlled records.

nodes.label: Assurance Integration Exchanges Sealed Submissions
nodes.source_location: # Assurance integration exchanges sealed submissions
nodes.rationale: Separate products exchange immutable digest-bound values instead of sharing stores, tables, or writable paths.

nodes.label: Assessment State and Security Verdict Are Separate
nodes.source_location: # Assessment State and Security Verdict are separate
nodes.rationale: Operational progress and resumability must not be confused with a sealed security conclusion.

nodes.label: Standalone Use Exposes Assessment Control, Not a Second Mission System
nodes.source_location: # Standalone use exposes Assessment control, not a second Mission system
nodes.rationale: Standalone operations control the shared Assessment Engine without duplicating Control Plane Mission or Quality Gate concepts.

nodes.label: V1 Assessment Is Read Only
nodes.source_location: # V1 assessment is read-only
nodes.rationale: Assessment may propose remediation, but subject mutation belongs to a separately authorized workflow and a later independently assessed subject.

nodes.label: Host Policy Controls Provider Activation
nodes.source_location: # Host Policy controls Provider activation
nodes.rationale: Installation or registration grants no obligation; the host freezes activation and providers cannot weaken the plan.

nodes.label: Machine Providers Have Explicit Assessor Identity
nodes.source_location: # Machine Providers have explicit Assessor identity
nodes.rationale: Machine provider lineage must be explicit and cannot impersonate independent agent or human review.

nodes.label: Provider Capability Describes Support but Grants No Permission
nodes.source_location: # Provider Capability describes support but grants no permission
nodes.rationale: Capability declarations inform policy and composition but never authorize access to code, processes, or networks.

nodes.label: Gate-bearing assessment requires bounded execution
nodes.rationale: Provider work must run in a bounded execution context; a backend whose identity, execution, coverage, or evidence cannot be bounded may contribute only advisory findings.

nodes.label: Provider Composition is frozen into the Assessment Seal
nodes.rationale: The seal binds every component that can affect assessment semantics, so changing any bound component requires a new assessment.

nodes.label: Coverage is proven against a frozen Plan
nodes.rationale: Coverage must be reconciled against a deterministic plan derived before analysis; an unsupported mandatory item prevents a satisfied verdict.

nodes.label: Assessment executes as a durable phase graph
nodes.rationale: Assessment work is persisted as an evidence-producing dependency graph rather than one long agent conversation.

nodes.label: Assessment Modes bound the breadth of security claims
nodes.rationale: Repository, Change, and Targeted modes bind different subjects and may not imply broader coverage without policy-authorized baseline evidence.

nodes.label: Policy layers may strengthen but not weaken the baseline
nodes.rationale: Policy layers compose monotonically and unknown, contradictory, or uncompilable requirements fail closed.

nodes.label: Analyzers enter through a versioned startup Registry
nodes.rationale: Analyzer capabilities, schemas, budgets, and runtime conditions must be declared before assessment creation; mid-assessment loading is forbidden.

nodes.label: Provider unavailability is distinct from an invalid contribution
nodes.rationale: Optional unavailability is diagnostic, structural invalidity causes safe read-only startup, and loss of a frozen provider blocks the assessment without substitution.

nodes.label: Analyzer failure requires explicit Resume
nodes.rationale: Analyzer attempts are durable and budget charged; failure blocks the assessment and only explicit resume may create another attempt under the same frozen inputs.

nodes.label: Cancellation preserves partial Evidence but produces no Verdict
nodes.rationale: Cancellation fences further execution and preserves partial evidence, but the canceled assessment has no security verdict.

nodes.label: Only sealed Assessments produce Assurance Submissions
nodes.rationale: Only an integrity-valid sealed assessment may submit an assurance result; blocked or canceled work remains an operational failure.

nodes.label: Severity, confidence, and Policy Significance are independent
nodes.rationale: Technical severity, evidence confidence, and policy significance record different meanings and must not be collapsed into scanner labels or aggregate scores.

nodes.label: Risk Acceptance is authorized, scoped, and non-destructive
nodes.rationale: Risk acceptance is immutable, authorized, and precisely bound; it may alter policy significance but cannot erase or downgrade the underlying finding.

nodes.label: V1 has one complete Supported Ecosystem
nodes.rationale: Complete V1 coverage claims are limited to TypeScript, JavaScript, and Node.js until tested analyzers and coverage contracts extend the support matrix.

nodes.label: Standard and Deep share Policy but differ in variance reduction
nodes.rationale: Both profiles enforce the same policy and verdict rules, while Deep adds independent discovery and validation lineages until a frozen convergence or budget condition.

nodes.label: Specialist agents remain subordinate to the Assessment Engine
nodes.rationale: Specialist roles may contribute candidates and evidence but cannot mutate policy, grant waivers, modify the subject, or decide the verdict.

nodes.label: Threat Models are versioned Evidence
nodes.rationale: Threat models are first-class evidence artifacts and may be reused only under exact identity, inventory, policy, and reuse-contract compatibility.

nodes.label: Change Assessment covers an impact cone, not only diff lines
nodes.rationale: Change assessment expands the exact diff across dependent code, trust boundaries, permissions, configuration, and tests; an unprovable cone yields expansion or indeterminate coverage.

nodes.label: Findings require explicit Validation state
nodes.rationale: Candidate findings must become validated, rejected with counter-evidence, or unresolved under an eligible evidence contract.

nodes.label: Source and Evidence egress is deny by default
nodes.rationale: Remote analyzers receive only authorized minimum source slices under a frozen egress contract, and secrets never enter remote inputs or human-readable reports.

nodes.label: Cross-Assessment Evidence reuse is contract-verified
nodes.rationale: Prior evidence is reusable only when its contract proves lineage, digests, policy, provider composition, schema, validity, and impact compatibility; reused records enter the new seal.

Codex Security Capability Breadth Is a Reference Envelope
nodes.rationale: Use publicly documented Codex Security breadth as a reference while redefining behavior and authority through DSH public contracts.

nodes.label: Finding Identity Is Local and Lineage Is Explicit
nodes.rationale: Prevent scanner identifiers or fuzzy similarity from automatically merging, closing, or mutating findings across assessments.

nodes.label: Validation Is Governed by Weakness-Specific Contracts
nodes.rationale: Require weakness-specific proof and explicit proof gaps because model confidence or scanner labels alone are insufficient.

nodes.label: Attack Paths Are Evidence Graphs, Not Dismissal Prerequisites
nodes.rationale: Use reachability and exploit chains where policy requires them without erasing independently proven local violations.

nodes.label: Remediation Cases Own One Primary Finding
nodes.rationale: Preserve independent verification and closure so one broad patch task cannot silently resolve an entire report.

nodes.label: Hardening Portfolios Are Non-Mutating Design Evidence
nodes.rationale: Keep structural hardening as design evidence and require separately authorized engineering work for mutation.

nodes.label: Canonical Assessment Bundles Are Machine-Authoritative
nodes.rationale: Make sealed versioned machine records authoritative while treating reports and interchange formats as derived views.

nodes.label: External Tracking Is Payload-Reviewed and Receipted
nodes.rationale: Require exact-payload review, destination identity, disclosure review, single-use authorization, and a returned receipt before external writes.

nodes.label: All Product Surfaces Share One Public Service Contract
nodes.rationale: Avoid parallel state by routing plugin, workbench, CLI, SDK, batch, and CI behavior through one service and assessment engine.

nodes.label: Technical Severity Is Normalized by Frozen Rules
nodes.rationale: Normalize severity from evidence-backed factors and retain scanner or industry scores as metadata rather than verdict authority.

nodes.label: Default Policy Blocks High Risk and Material Uncertainty
nodes.rationale: Block validated high risk and material unresolved uncertainty while allowing hosts to strengthen but not weaken the safety ceiling.

nodes.label: Risk Acceptance Has Severity and Authority Ceilings
nodes.rationale: Constrain acceptance by severity, independent authority, rationale, controls, and expiry while prohibiting self-acceptance.

nodes.label: Patch Generation and Application Use Separate Authority
nodes.rationale: Separate non-mutating patch creation from digest-bound application authority and reject stale subjects or altered patches.

nodes.label: Finding Resolution Requires a New Sealed Assessment
nodes.rationale: Patch application alone cannot close a finding; only independently verified evidence in a new sealed assessment can establish resolution lineage.

nodes.label: Reproducers Never Target Production or Real Credentials
nodes.rationale: Confine validation to safe isolated environments and record an explicit proof gap instead of executing unsafe tests.

nodes.label: Sensitive Evidence Is Protected and Secrets Are Never Retained
nodes.rationale: Encrypt sensitive evidence under versioned policy, fail safely when keys are unavailable, and retain only irreversible secret fingerprints with minimum context.

nodes.label: Exports Use Audience-Specific Redaction Profiles
nodes.rationale: Tailor derived exports by audience while preserving provenance references and withholding original credentials and canonical authority.

nodes.label: Sealed Bundles Are Never Migrated in Place
nodes.rationale: Keep sealed bundles byte-stable, derive provenance-bound normalized views, and fail closed on incompatible schemas.

nodes.label: Retention Purges Payloads with Auditable Tombstones
nodes.rationale: Allow exact-authority payload destruction while retaining auditable identity and digest records and forbidding fuzzy or bulk deletion.

nodes.label: Product Proof Separates Conformance from Effectiveness
nodes.rationale: Keep deterministic capability conformance distinct from independently measured security effectiveness; demonstrations and feedback supplement neither proof program.

nodes.label: Ground Truth Is Hidden and Independently Adjudicated
nodes.rationale: Prevent evaluation leakage and single-source bias through sealed hidden truth, independent adjudication, deterministic evidence, and appropriate external tools.

Benchmarks Use Four Complementary Corpus Lanes
nodes.source_location: # Benchmarks use four complementary Corpus Lanes
nodes.rationale: Complementary deterministic, seeded, historical-pair, and negative-control lanes provide stronger truth than findings from random repositories.

nodes.label: Effectiveness Compares Fixed Baseline and Product Arms
nodes.source_location: # Effectiveness compares fixed baseline and product Arms
nodes.rationale: Fixed comparison arms and matched-budget views expose both security performance and the additional compute used to obtain it.

nodes.label: Effectiveness Prioritizes Validated Risk and Honest Indeterminacy
nodes.source_location: # Effectiveness prioritizes validated risk and honest indeterminacy
nodes.rationale: Validated recall, precision, unsafe satisfaction, and coverage honesty measure safety better than finding volume or model confidence.

nodes.label: Utility Measures Risk Reduction Against Human and Runtime Cost
nodes.source_location: # Utility measures risk reduction against human and runtime cost
nodes.rationale: Utility must connect validated risk reduction and remediation outcomes to elapsed time, runtime cost, and human effort.

nodes.label: Stochastic Evaluation Reports Distributions, Not Best Runs
nodes.source_location: # Stochastic evaluation reports distributions, not best runs
nodes.rationale: Frozen independent repetitions and distribution statistics prevent cherry-picking favorable stochastic runs.

nodes.label: Ground Truth Leakage Invalidates the Evaluation Run
nodes.source_location: # Ground Truth leakage invalidates the Evaluation Run
nodes.rationale: Any leakage of hidden defects, seed identity, or expected findings contaminates the entire run and cannot be repaired by selective result removal.

nodes.label: Capability Conformance Is a Reusable Provider Contract Kit
nodes.source_location: # Capability Conformance is a reusable Provider contract kit
nodes.rationale: Built-in and third-party providers must prove the same applicable command, state, evidence, recovery, authority, and packaging contracts.

nodes.label: Hostile Repositories Are First-Class Conformance Subjects
nodes.source_location: # Hostile repositories are first-class Conformance Subjects
nodes.rationale: Repository-controlled content must be tested as hostile data that can attempt injection, path escape, forgery, policy weakening, or resource exhaustion.

nodes.label: Evaluation Runs Are Immutable and Pre-Registered
nodes.source_location: # Evaluation Runs are immutable and pre-registered
nodes.rationale: Immutable run bundles and pre-frozen definitions prevent post-hoc changes that would make an experiment appear to pass.

nodes.label: Development, Qualification, and Release Corpora Are Separated
nodes.source_location: # Development, Qualification, and Release Corpora are separated
nodes.rationale: Tuning, milestone qualification, and release promotion require distinct corpus partitions so exposed evidence cannot prove generalization.

nodes.label: Ground Truth Adjudication Is Blinded and Independent
nodes.source_location: # Ground Truth adjudication is blinded and independent
nodes.rationale: Independent blinded review with preserved disagreement and tie-break evidence prevents arm identity from biasing finding matches.

nodes.label: Finding Matching Is Predeclared and One-to-One
nodes.source_location: # Finding matching is predeclared and one-to-one
nodes.rationale: Predeclared semantic matching and one-to-one assignment prevent duplicate findings or post-hoc judgment from inflating recall.

nodes.label: Insufficient Benchmark Strata Are Inconclusive
nodes.source_location: # Insufficient Benchmark strata are inconclusive
nodes.rationale: Each severity, weakness, mode, and ecosystem stratum must independently satisfy sample and uncertainty requirements.

nodes.label: Proof Runs in PR, Nightly, Weekly, and RC Tiers
nodes.source_location: # Proof runs in PR, Nightly, Weekly, and RC tiers
nodes.rationale: Progressively broader proof tiers culminate in sealed holdout, all-arm, packed-installation, and blinded-adjudication evidence for release candidates.

nodes.label: Model and Provider Drift Requires Requalification
nodes.source_location: # Model and Provider drift requires requalification
nodes.rationale: Effectiveness evidence binds exact deployment and composition; any drift changes the evaluated arm and requires fresh qualification.

nodes.label: Benchmark Failures and Reruns Are Preclassified
nodes.source_location: # Benchmark failures and reruns are preclassified
nodes.rationale: Product failures count against their arm, while proven benchmark failures invalidate the case uniformly; selective reruns and reclassification are forbidden.

nodes.label: Benchmark Major Changes Require Bridge Runs
nodes.source_location: # Benchmark major changes require Bridge Runs
nodes.rationale: Breaking measurement changes require controlled overlap before historical and current results may be compared.

nodes.label: Evaluation Budgets Include Compute, Network, and Human Cost
nodes.source_location: # Evaluation Budgets include compute, network, and human cost
nodes.rationale: Every arm must freeze and report resource and human limits so quality and efficiency can be compared honestly.

nodes.label: Dogfood Can Block Release but Cannot Prove Effectiveness
nodes.source_location: # Dogfood can block release but cannot prove Effectiveness
nodes.rationale: Operational findings may expose release-blocking defects, but unknown ground truth prevents dogfood from replacing hidden-corpus effectiveness proof.

nodes.label: Release Thresholds Combine Hard Floors and Pre-Holdout Calibration
nodes.source_location: # Release Thresholds combine hard floors and pre-Holdout calibration
nodes.rationale: Non-negotiable safety floors and pre-holdout calibrated statistical thresholds prevent unsafe or post-hoc release promotion.

nodes.label: Exposed Release Holdouts Are Retired After a Failed Candidate
nodes.source_location: # Exposed Release Holdouts are retired after a failed Candidate
nodes.rationale: A candidate changed after holdout exposure must use a fresh hidden partition; repeated attempts on the same answers cannot prove generalization.

Releases must be non-inferior in every mandatory stratum
nodes.rationale: A candidate must meet pre-registered non-inferiority margins in each mandatory risk, weakness, mode, and platform stratum; aggregate gains cannot hide a regression.

nodes.label: The first public Candidate is 0.1.0-rc.1
nodes.rationale: The independently versioned product begins public candidacy at 0.1.0-rc.1 and promotes to 0.1.0 only after every release gate passes.

nodes.label: Public security claims are Evidence- and scope-bound
nodes.rationale: Every public support claim must name its ecosystem, mode, profile, policy, matrix, evaluation versions, providers, metrics, costs, uncertainty, and omissions.

nodes.label: The security product has a stricter self-security Release Gate
nodes.rationale: Release requires zero confirmed critical or high self-findings, and medium findings affecting foundational assurance properties block by default.

nodes.label: Stable support requires Windows, Linux, and macOS proof
nodes.rationale: Stable 0.1.0 core capability requires packed-install and conformance evidence on all three supported desktop platforms.

nodes.label: Security Telemetry is off by default and aggregate only
nodes.rationale: Telemetry requires opt-in, contains only versioned aggregate operations data, and excludes source, paths, findings, evidence, credentials, ground truth, and other sensitive content.

nodes.label: Public Scorecards prove method without exposing Holdouts
nodes.rationale: A redacted scorecard exposes enough method, metrics, uncertainty, budgets, limits, and failures to assess evidence strength without disclosing holdout answers or sensitive evidence.

nodes.label: Stable promotion uses the exact qualified build
nodes.rationale: Stable promotion preserves qualified behavior byte-for-byte except for version, signature, and release metadata; behavioral changes require a new RC and rerun gates.

nodes.label: Security Assurance ships as one bundle with independent entry points
nodes.rationale: One npm and plugin product exposes independently activatable service, tool, provider, workbench, invariant, and generated-contract entry points until real deployment pressure justifies package splits.

nodes.label: Public names identify Security Assurance
nodes.rationale: The package, Cordis capability, and Remote namespace use Security Assurance-specific names to preserve the product's independent authority boundary.

nodes.label: Installed Security entry points are dormant by default
nodes.rationale: Installation contributes dormant capability rows; a deployment owner enables them only after all policy, protection, execution, budget, mapping, and integration configuration is complete.

nodes.label: One Security Service exposes explicit domain operations
nodes.rationale: A single public strongly typed service exposes explicit Assessment, Remediation, and Delivery commands and queries while their deep modules remain separate behind it.

nodes.label: Assessment start publishes a durable receipt
nodes.rationale: startAssessment returns only after durable creation commits; after receipt publication the engine owns execution and later lifecycle changes use explicit operations.

nodes.label: Security mutations use branded identities revisions and idempotency
nodes.rationale: State-changing commands carry opaque identities, idempotency keys, and expected revisions so duplicates return committed outcomes and stale writes fail without mutation.

nodes.label: Interrupted Analyzer attempts require explicit resume
nodes.rationale: Recovery never silently re-executes an analyzer attempt; an interrupted attempt blocks the assessment until authorized resume creates a new budgeted attempt with distinct provenance.

nodes.label: Frozen Provider Composition survives hot replacement
nodes.rationale: Accepted assessments own their exact provider and analyzer handles; hot replacement affects new admission only, and plugin unloading waits for owned work to quiesce.

nodes.label: Security Role Agents are orchestrated directly through Subagents
nodes.rationale: The durable Assessment Engine invokes ctx.subagents with frozen prompts, restrictions, schemas, provider selection, and budgets and records every admitted and settled contribution.

nodes.label: Workbench uses package-owned Typert remotes
nodes.rationale: Generated package-owned Typert and Remote contracts let Workbench invoke explicit service operations without central API changes, ad hoc REST, or browser access to storage and evidence paths.

nodes.label: Workbench is an additive Harness Web surface
nodes.rationale: Workbench contributes through launcher and overlay slots without replacing Harness UI owners, while the host service remains usable without client slots.

nodes.label: Workbench progress is revision-driven long polling
nodes.rationale: A bounded cancellable Typert wait-for-revision operation drives immutable snapshot refresh and safe reconnect without a plugin-specific SSE or WebSocket protocol.

nodes.label: Security Assurance Plugin Boundary
nodes.rationale: The independent plugin integrates only through public Harness seams and neither modifies Harness Core nor patches agent-loop, forks Harness, or copies Harness source.

Security Service Is Sole Mutation Boundary
nodes.rationale: Centralize every authoritative state change behind one contract that enforces authorization, revision, idempotency, and evidence checks.

nodes.label: Assessment Subject Sources Are Explicit and Immutable
nodes.rationale: Freeze exact source identity before admission and reject mutable aliases or partial representations as authoritative subjects.

nodes.label: Analyzers Read Only Content-Addressed Subject Snapshots
nodes.rationale: Ensure analyzers observe immutable bytes by materializing a canonical read-only snapshot instead of reading the original workspace.

nodes.label: Special Repository Objects Never Expand Implicitly
nodes.rationale: Bound symlink, submodule, and archive behavior so repository structure cannot silently enlarge the assessed subject.

nodes.label: Security Private State Lives Under DSH Home
nodes.rationale: Keep authoritative security state out of target repositories and require a separate authorized delivery operation for exports.

nodes.label: Assessment Execution Uses Revision CAS, Leases, and Fencing
nodes.rationale: Permit concurrent inspection while ensuring only the current fenced lease holder can advance an assessment.

nodes.label: Sensitive Evidence Requires an Explicit Key Provider
nodes.rationale: Fail into read-only safe mode rather than generate or retain plaintext key material when required encryption is unavailable.

nodes.label: Analyzer Execution Class Determines Verdict Eligibility
nodes.rationale: Derive verdict eligibility from proven execution and evidence boundaries rather than registration alone.

nodes.label: v0.1 Gate-Bearing Local Analyzers Use Bounded Harness Capabilities
nodes.rationale: Limit local analyzers to narrow immutable inputs and bounded filesystem, process, and sandbox capabilities; unsupported isolation leaves advisory or indeterminate results.

nodes.label: Model Egress Uses Minimal Redacted Source Slices
nodes.rationale: Constrain model disclosure to purpose-specific redacted slices and deny verdict-eligible execution when the egress contract cannot be met.

nodes.label: TS JS Node Support Uses a Hybrid Analyzer Portfolio
nodes.rationale: Combine deterministic analysis with governed role agents while subjecting third-party scanners to the same qualification contracts.

nodes.label: Dependency Advisories Are Versioned Offline Snapshots
nodes.rationale: Freeze signed advisory intelligence into provider composition so assessment evidence remains reproducible and independent of live network responses.

nodes.label: Standard and Deep Have Explicit Qualified Analysis Paths
nodes.rationale: Make Deep a larger independently cross-checked analysis plan under unchanged policy semantics rather than a model effort setting.

nodes.label: Required Analyzer Failure Cannot Become Security Failure or Satisfaction
nodes.rationale: Represent missing required execution as blocked or indeterminate, never as proof of security failure or satisfaction.

nodes.label: Repository Content Is Untrusted Data, Not Instruction
nodes.rationale: Prevent repository-controlled text from changing analyzers, providers, policy, egress, tools, or role instructions.

nodes.label: First Release Candidate Proves the Read-Only Assessment Core
nodes.rationale: Concentrate qualification evidence on the complete read-only core before adding remediation, tracking, and additional product surfaces.

nodes.label: First Harness Compatibility Target Is Exact 0.1.1-rc.2
nodes.rationale: Claim compatibility one exact Harness version at a time only after packed-profile and operating-system evidence.

nodes.label: Security Authority Is Derived from the Real Caller Channel
nodes.rationale: Derive identity and authority from trusted host channels and fail closed rather than trusting caller-supplied permissions or scope.

nodes.label: Assessment Subjects Come from a Host-Owned Repository Registry
nodes.rationale: Restrict assessments to pre-authorized repository identities whose roots and security bindings are owned by the host.

nodes.label: Start Requests Reference Host-Resolved Security Configuration
nodes.rationale: Keep start requests declarative and narrow while resolving paths, policies, providers, budgets, evidence rules, and immutable snapshots from host-owned configuration.

nodes.label: Security Service Exposes Fixed Commands and Bounded Queries
nodes.rationale: Expose an explicit typed surface and keep authority, scope, state, revision, and disclosure checks inside the service boundary.

Only Coverage Reconciliation Can Seal INDETERMINATE
nodes.source_location: # Only Coverage Reconciliation can seal INDETERMINATE
nodes.rationale: Recoverable failures remain BLOCKED; deterministic reconciliation may seal indeterminate only after proving no eligible path remains or the frozen budget is exhausted.

nodes.label: Cancellation Commits Only After Proven Quiescence
nodes.source_location: # Cancellation commits only after proven quiescence
nodes.rationale: CANCELED is truthful only after all assessment-owned work is durably unable to publish or mutate state.

nodes.label: Resume Preserves the Frozen Assessment Contract
nodes.source_location: # Resume preserves the frozen Assessment contract
nodes.rationale: Resume may create attempts only for incomplete eligible work under the original subject, policy, plan, composition, and budget; semantic changes require a new Assessment.

nodes.label: Risk Acceptance Occurs Before Seal in a Decision Window
nodes.source_location: # Risk Acceptance occurs before Seal in a decision window
nodes.rationale: Risk decisions are permitted only in an explicit pre-seal BLOCKED window and can never rewrite a sealed historical assessment.

nodes.label: Risk Acceptance Requires Human or Control Plane Decision Authority
nodes.source_location: # Risk Acceptance requires human or Control Plane Decision Authority
nodes.rationale: Models, role agents, analyzers, and ordinary callers cannot accept risk; critical break-glass requires two distinct qualified human authorities.

nodes.label: Official Exports Require a SEALED Assessment
nodes.source_location: # Official exports require a SEALED Assessment
nodes.rationale: Only sealed assessments may produce canonical bundles, official exports, or Control Plane submissions; diagnostic views remain non-authoritative.

nodes.label: Seal, Verdict, Bundle, and Submission Commit Atomically
nodes.source_location: # Seal, Verdict, Bundle, and Submission commit atomically
nodes.rationale: A SEALED state exists only when verified immutable artifacts and their exact digests commit with Seal, Verdict, Bundle Manifest, Submission identity, and final revision.

nodes.label: Model Tools Expose Explicit Assessment Operations Without Risk Acceptance
nodes.source_location: # Model tools expose explicit Assessment operations without Risk Acceptance
nodes.rationale: Separate bounded tools delegate to the Security Service; there is no generic command, repository administration, or model Risk Acceptance tool.

nodes.label: Model Results Are Bounded and Redacted by Default
nodes.source_location: # Model results are bounded and redacted by default
nodes.rationale: Service-enforced pagination, size limits, and redaction prevent sensitive evidence and protected source from entering model history by default.

nodes.label: Third-Party Analyzers Register Through the Security Service
nodes.source_location: # Third-party analyzers register through the Security Service
nodes.rationale: Validated fiber-owned registration freezes exact analyzer identity and capability while rejecting duplicate or contradictory descriptors before execution.

nodes.label: Config Replacement Quiesces Before Recovery
nodes.source_location: # Config replacement quiesces before recovery
nodes.rationale: The old Service closes admission and records interruptions before unload; replacement recovers durably without silently migrating or resuming frozen assessments.

nodes.label: Assessment Aggregate Has a Narrow Consistency Boundary
nodes.source_location: # Assessment Aggregate has a narrow consistency boundary
nodes.rationale: Lifecycle, attempts, findings, coverage, decisions, verdict, and seal share one aggregate, while repositories, evidence payloads, remediation, and delivery remain separate identity-bound boundaries.

nodes.label: Persistence Combines a Revision Journal with Current Projections
nodes.source_location: # Persistence combines a Revision Journal with current projections
nodes.rationale: Each mutation appends immutable provenance and updates its bounded read projection in the same SQLite transaction so they cannot disagree.

nodes.label: Commands Publish Durable Work Transactionally
nodes.source_location: # Commands publish durable work transactionally
nodes.rationale: Command outcome, revision, and outbox work commit together so crashes create neither orphan state nor lost in-memory callbacks.

nodes.label: Revisions Advance Once per Externally Observable Transaction
nodes.source_location: # Revisions advance once per externally observable transaction
nodes.rationale: Revision measures committed domain change rather than row-write volume and supports optimistic concurrency and long polling.

nodes.label: Idempotency Binds Authority, Operation, Target, and Request
nodes.source_location: # Idempotency binds authority operation target and request
nodes.rationale: A repeated equivalent mutation returns its original outcome, while key reuse under different effective content fails closed without mutation.

nodes.label: State Transitions Are Exhaustive and Declarative
nodes.source_location: # State transitions are exhaustive and declarative
nodes.rationale: One Kernel-owned matrix defines every legal transition and rejection, preventing Service methods from inventing independent lifecycle semantics.

nodes.label: Execution May Repeat but Result Admission Is at Most Once
nodes.source_location: # Execution may repeat but result admission is at most once
nodes.rationale: Physical analyzer execution may repeat after failure, but fenced idempotent compare-and-swap admits each terminal result no more than once.

nodes.label: Evidence Enters Through Staged Verified Publication
nodes.source_location: # Evidence enters through staged verified publication
nodes.rationale: Untrusted producers receive bounded staging only; the Service validates and protects bytes before atomically publishing an immutable evidence identity and digest.

nodes.label: Digests Use Versioned Deterministic Envelopes
nodes.source_location: # Digests use versioned deterministic envelopes
nodes.rationale: Versioned algorithm, media, length, and canonicalization metadata make content identities deterministic without reinterpreting older digests.

nodes.label: Wait for revision is bounded cancellable and transaction-free
nodes.rationale: Revision waiting is bounded, cancellable, rate limited, repeatable from the returned revision, and holds no transaction, lock, lease, or privileged store object.

nodes.label: Public errors are stable typed and redacted
nodes.rationale: Public failures use a versioned stable envelope while sensitive paths, evidence, secrets, payloads, traces, and unauthorized-resource existence remain private.

nodes.label: Analyzer identity binds version schema and build
nodes.rationale: Stable analyzer identity combines namespaced ID, implementation version, descriptor schema version, and integrity-bound build digest across registration, attempts, lineage, qualification, and seals.

nodes.label: Analyzer Descriptors are frozen validated pure data
nodes.rationale: Admission uses a deeply frozen JSON-safe validated descriptor containing only declarative claims; executable construction remains in a separate factory.

nodes.label: Analyzer capabilities use a versioned taxonomy
nodes.rationale: Capability claims use a versioned core vocabulary; unknown mandatory meanings fail composition while optional extensions remain non-authoritative metadata.

nodes.label: The Kernel computes and freezes Verdict Eligibility
nodes.rationale: The kernel computes immutable eligibility from validated identity, qualification, provider, probe, policy, contracts, boundary, and runtime conditions; analyzers cannot self-declare eligibility.

nodes.label: Analyzer instances are Attempt-scoped and disposable
nodes.rationale: Each durable attempt owns a fresh analyzer instance and every resource it obtains; every terminal or recovery path requires disposal or durable proof that quiescence is unknown.

nodes.label: Analyzer inputs are immutable bounded and authority-free
nodes.rationale: AnalyzerInput freezes semantic task data without ambient host authority; executable access is separately supplied through execution-class capability handles.

nodes.label: Analyzer Contributions are versioned and cannot decide Verdicts
nodes.rationale: A bounded versioned contribution is validated before admission and reconciled by the kernel; it cannot mutate state, grant acceptance, decide verdicts, seal, submit, or trigger arbitrary work.

nodes.label: Runner progress events are bounded and non-authoritative
nodes.rationale: Rate- and size-limited events report progress but cannot affect findings, coverage, budget, or authoritative state; only the terminal contribution is semantic output.

nodes.label: Attempt cancellation fences late results and requires cleanup
nodes.rationale: Cancellation durably closes admission before signaling abort, rejects stale results, and requires bounded backend termination plus disposal evidence or blocks the assessment.

nodes.label: The Kernel reserves and meters nested Attempt budgets
nodes.rationale: The kernel reserves maximum attempt budget before execution and service-owned handles meter all nested work against that authority until settlement.

nodes.label: Scheduling enforces hierarchical fair concurrency
nodes.rationale: The service scheduler is the only admission path and applies a frozen hierarchical concurrency envelope with bounded fair queues.

nodes.label: In-process extensions are trusted Host code not a sandbox
nodes.rationale: In-process JavaScript has ambient host authority; descriptors and handles govern integration but do not create a sandbox, so untrusted code requires a qualified isolation backend.

nodes.label: Analyzers receive only Attempt-scoped Capability Handles
nodes.rationale: Opaque minimum-privilege handles bind execution authority to attempt identity, budget, deadline, and fence and reject use after settlement or transfer.

nodes.label: External network access passes through governed brokers
nodes.rationale: Gate-bearing analyzers have no ambient network path and may reach external services only through qualified, quota-bound, audited egress brokers under frozen contracts.

nodes.label: Authoritative Contributions are not reused across Assessments in v0.1
nodes.rationale: Every gate-bearing assessment executes and admits a fresh contribution with new lineage and budget; non-authoritative parse cache affects performance only.

nodes.label: Gate-bearing Analyzers require scoped Qualification Records
nodes.rationale: Gate-bearing status requires a current host-trusted qualification record for the exact analyzer identity and build across capability, isolation, evidence, failure, effectiveness, provider, platform, and scope constraints.

nodes.label: Role Agents Receive Minimal Context Grants
nodes.rationale: Limit each role to purpose-specific data and reauthorize any additional source material against containment, disclosure, and budget controls.

nodes.label: Each Role Attempt Uses a Fresh Isolated Subagent Session
nodes.rationale: Prevent hidden conversational state from contaminating durable role execution and protect transcripts as governed evidence.

nodes.label: Role Tools Are Fixed Least-Privilege Manifests
nodes.rationale: Expose only attempt-scoped capabilities and exclude generic shell, network, mutation, service, risk, and store access.

nodes.label: Role Agents Request Follow-Up Work Through the Kernel
nodes.rationale: Prevent recursive self-authorization by requiring bounded follow-up proposals to pass kernel policy, independence, concurrency, and budget checks.

nodes.label: Roles Communicate Through Immutable Governed Artifacts
nodes.rationale: Preserve provenance and disclosure controls by replacing mutable inter-agent memory and chat with admitted artifacts and bounded projections.

nodes.label: Deep Independent Passes Remain Blind Until Initial Submission
nodes.rationale: Protect meaningful independence by freezing initial contributions before correlation or challenge begins.

nodes.label: Cross-Challenge Never Rewrites an Original Contribution
nodes.rationale: Keep challenges separately attributable so corroboration, disputes, and proof gaps cannot erase the claims they examine.

nodes.label: Evidence Contracts, Not Agent Votes, Determine Convergence
nodes.rationale: Base claim resolution on deterministic evidence and coverage contracts, leaving disagreement unresolved rather than synthesizing consensus.

nodes.label: Role Contributions Are Versioned Structured Proposals
nodes.rationale: Admit bounded structured proposals while reserving finding, severity, policy, risk, verdict, seal, and mutation decisions for authoritative services.

nodes.label: Malformed Role Output Allows at Most One Governed Format Repair
nodes.rationale: Allow one syntax-only, traceable repair while rejecting heuristic extraction, new claims, and partial admission.

nodes.label: Model Invocations Have Complete Protected Lineage
nodes.rationale: Record complete invocation identity and usage in canonical lineage while protecting sensitive payloads under retention and disclosure policy.

nodes.label: Required Role Failure Blocks Until Explicit Resume
nodes.rationale: Preserve successful work and failed lineage while prohibiting silent retry, model substitution, weakened independence, or discarded evidence.

nodes.label: Deterministic-Only Profiles Are Explicit and Cannot Impersonate Agent Coverage
nodes.rationale: Distinguish qualified deterministic capability from model-assisted coverage and block rather than relabel output when required role providers are unavailable.

nodes.label: Candidates Remain Immutable and Validation Creates Separate Outcomes
nodes.rationale: Preserve original candidate identity and contradictory evidence while linking separate validation outcomes and resulting finding states.

nodes.label: Candidate Admission Enforces Schema, Provenance, Anchors, and Bounds
nodes.rationale: Keep invalid, unauthenticated, stale, oversized, or out-of-subject proposals out of validation, coverage, deduplication, and reporting.

nodes.label: Candidate Clusters Never Merge Evidence Automatically
nodes.rationale: Use clustering only for review efficiency and require governed adjudication before consolidation, preserving each claim and evidence lineage.

nodes.label: Finding Changes Append Revisions and Sealed Versions Remain Immutable
nodes.rationale: Maintain append-only finding history and require linked records or a new assessment after sealing instead of rewriting prior findings.

nodes.label: Policy Layers Preserve Source Identity and Trust

nodes.label: Coverage Claims are proposals and the Kernel resolves them
nodes.rationale: Producer claims do not establish coverage; the kernel independently verifies admission, obligation rules, eligibility, evidence, independence, overflow, gaps, and lineage.

nodes.label: Obligations resolve as SATISFIED, NOT_APPLICABLE, or GAP
nodes.rationale: Every obligation reaches exactly one evidenced terminal resolution before sealing; percentages, process success, and absence of findings are not resolution states.

nodes.label: NOT_APPLICABLE requires eligible negative proof
nodes.rationale: Non-applicability requires qualified inventory, scope selection, and negative evidence tied to the exact selector and plan version; later contradictory facts require a new resolution.

nodes.label: Coverage hierarchy requires every mandatory child
nodes.rationale: A parent is satisfied only when each mandatory descendant is satisfied or independently proved not applicable; aggregate strength cannot mask a child gap.

nodes.label: Advisory work cannot compensate for mandatory gaps
nodes.rationale: Optional breadth may enrich evidence but cannot satisfy, downgrade, weight away, or hide a mandatory coverage gap.

nodes.label: Policy Significance is derived by a deterministic rule trace
nodes.rationale: Policy significance is deterministically derived from exact policy, scope, severity, confidence, lineage, risk acceptance, and controls with every input preserved in a trace.

nodes.label: Policy Evaluation uses one recorded instant
nodes.rationale: All freshness and expiry rules in final evaluation use one committed host-provided instant rather than ambient clocks.

nodes.label: A proven blocking violation takes precedence over incomplete Coverage
nodes.rationale: A proved unaccepted blocking finding yields FAILED despite gaps; absent such proof, mandatory gaps yield INDETERMINATE and only complete mandatory coverage without blockers yields SATISFIED.

nodes.label: The Policy Evaluator is pure and emits a complete trace
nodes.rationale: Equal frozen canonical inputs under one evaluator version produce byte-equivalent verdict candidates and traces without I/O, time, provider, model, or state-transition effects.

nodes.label: Sealing requires an independent deterministic Readiness Check
nodes.rationale: An independent kernel check verifies terminal work, resolved obligations, closed authority, consistent revisions and chains, trace agreement, and generatable artifacts before atomic sealing.

nodes.label: Release Conformance targets a packed fresh Harness installation
nodes.rationale: Release proof installs the exact packed artifact into a fresh declared Harness profile and exercises public plugin boundaries; source aliases and modified trees cannot establish release claims.

nodes.label: The Reference Test Host uses real Harness composition
nodes.rationale: The reference host uses actual Harness and Cordis loading, services, tools, remotes, client slots, and lifecycle with isolated per-test authority and no shared developer state.

nodes.label: Tests have no security semantic bypass
nodes.rationale: Production exposes no test-only weakening path; deterministic dependencies use authenticated official seams and forensic inspection remains read-only and out of process.

nodes.label: Deterministic Reference Fakes exercise official seams
nodes.rationale: Versioned fakes use real analyzer, provider, key, broker, and clock contracts to prove orchestration and failure conformance, but never count as effectiveness, qualification, claims, or customer evidence.

nodes.label: The Transition Matrix receives model-based Conformance
nodes.rationale: Generated valid and invalid public command sequences are predicted by the pure kernel model and compared with the packed service; shrunk failures become regressions.

nodes.label: Crash Conformance hard-kills at named persistence checkpoints
nodes.rationale: Crash proof terminates the complete host at non-authorizing durable checkpoints, restarts against the same isolated root, and verifies recovery artifacts, fencing, and blocked outcomes.

nodes.label: Multiprocess races prove CAS, leases, fencing, and sealing
nodes.rationale: At least two packed hosts race security operations against one authority root and must produce only permitted commits, fenced ownership, one semantic result, and one seal.

nodes.label: Adversarial filesystem proof is platform-specific
nodes.rationale: Qualified fixtures exercise platform-specific filesystem attacks and preserve distinct Windows, Linux, and macOS evidence and coverage outcomes.

nodes.label: Canonical security artifacts have reviewed Golden Vectors
nodes.rationale: Versioned reviewed golden vectors fix exact artifact bytes, digests, and reader semantics across platforms; intentional changes require compatibility analysis, review, regeneration, and fail-closed proof.

nodes.label: Ground Truth Is Unavailable to Scanning Runners

nodes.label: The Versioned Metrics Engine Has Synthetic Golden Oracles

nodes.label: Conformance Mutants Must Be Killed Before Release
nodes.rationale: Demonstrate that black-box tests detect removal or inversion of every mandatory security control before promotion.

nodes.label: Resource Proof Measures Limits, Leaks, and Recovery
nodes.rationale: Qualify bounded resource behavior, leak freedom, cancellation, restart reconciliation, and recovery instead of relying on average duration.

nodes.label: Release Evidence Manifests Bind Exact Artifacts to Proof
nodes.rationale: Bind exact packed and locked artifacts to all required proof identities and verify their digests against the release constitution.

nodes.label: Deterministic Failures Cannot Be Erased by Reruns
nodes.rationale: Preserve deterministic failures and complete model-assisted distributions so selective reruns cannot erase adverse product evidence.

nodes.label: Security Service Is the Sole External Business Interface
nodes.rationale: Give all callers leverage through one service contract while keeping kernel, engine, persistence, scheduling, and transaction internals package-private.

nodes.label: Security Service Is One Deep Module with Explicit Operations
nodes.rationale: Expose a small typed operation set while hiding authority resolution, lifecycle, kernel execution, transactions, evidence, redaction, and failure mapping.

nodes.label: Callers Act Through Resolver-Issued Security Invocations

nodes.label: Security Assessment Kernel Is a Pure Deep Module
nodes.rationale: Concentrate state and verdict rules in a deterministic, side-effect-free module over canonical immutable values.

nodes.label: Assessment Engine Is Package-Private and Hides Phase Orchestration
nodes.rationale: Hide scheduling and phase orchestration behind a narrow recovery, wake, bounded-progress, and quiescence interface.

nodes.label: SQLite Persistence Is a Package-Private Deep Module
nodes.rationale: Hide relational lifecycle, journals, projections, work queues, leases, migrations, CAS, and recovery without exposing repository or transaction primitives.

nodes.label: Evidence Persistence Is a Separate Package-Private Deep Module
nodes.rationale: Separate bounded protected payload handling from relational aggregate persistence and expose only small internal interfaces and bounded writers.

nodes.label: Seams Exist Only Where Multiple Adapters Justify Them
nodes.rationale: Create external seams only for genuinely variable behavior with concrete adapters, avoiding public ports invented solely for mocking.

nodes.label: Dependencies Point Inward Toward Domain Values and the Kernel
nodes.rationale: Keep domain and kernel independent of frameworks, storage, processes, browsers, adapters, and global service locators.

nodes.label: One Package Exposes Separated Runtime and Contract Entry Points
nodes.rationale: Preserve one product and npm unit while separating runtime consumers, contracts, conformance libraries, and generated workbench interfaces by export path.

nodes.rationale: Assessment queries expose immutable authority-filtered snapshots and redacted watermarked list items rather than journals, internals, private paths, diagnostics, or mutable objects.

nodes.label: Revision wait returns a change signal not an event stream
nodes.rationale: Revision wait reports only bounded change state and tells clients to refetch an authorized snapshot; it does not stream journals, patches, evidence, findings, logs, or subscriptions.

nodes.label: Resume and Cancel require revision, idempotency, and reason
nodes.rationale: Resume and cancel require exact identity, expected revision, idempotency, structured reason, and trusted invocation and cannot override frozen semantics or bypass cleanup.

nodes.label: Finding queries separate redacted summaries from revision detail
nodes.rationale: Finding lists return bounded redacted summaries while authorized detail exposes revisioned projections and disclosure-limited evidence metadata without mutable records.

nodes.label: Evidence disclosure is purpose- and Profile-bound
nodes.rationale: Evidence views re-evaluate invocation, purpose, profile, classification, keys, retention, redaction, egress, and byte limits and never expose reusable unrestricted storage authority.

nodes.label: Risk Decisions derive authority and Critical acceptance requires two
nodes.rationale: Risk authority comes only from trusted invocation, and critical break-glass acceptance requires two distinct qualified authorities submitting matching decisions.

nodes.label: Bundle Manifest is a View and Submission is self-contained
nodes.rationale: The bundle manifest is disclosure-filtered metadata, while a sealed assurance submission is an immutable digest-bound value sufficient for authorized validation and import without store access.

nodes.label: Exports use Host-registered destinations and durable Receipts
nodes.rationale: Export requests target registered destinations with bounded non-secret options and return durable receipts; access uses short-lived host capabilities rather than paths or caller credentials.

nodes.label: Mutations share a versioned idempotent CAS envelope
nodes.rationale: All mutations carry contract version and idempotency, existing aggregates also require exact revision, and canonical request replay returns the original receipt or a stable conflict without partial mutation.

nodes.label: Contract majors govern semantic compatibility
nodes.rationale: Public contract majors preserve field meaning, authority, defaults, and failures; breaking changes require a new major and sealed artifacts retain long-horizon compatibility without rewriting bytes.

nodes.label: Workbench is a Service Client not an authority
nodes.rationale: Workbench renders immutable service snapshots and submits catalogued commands under host authority while owning no lifecycle, evidence, decision, verdict, export, authorization, retry, store, or artifact semantics.

nodes.label: Workbench mounts as an additive launcher and overlay
nodes.rationale: The optional client contributes only launcher and overlay slots, leaves Harness owners untouched, and disposes all UI state and contributions under Fiber ownership.

nodes.label: Workbench information architecture is fixed for v0.1
nodes.rationale: Every fixed Workbench view projects public service operations and introduces no hidden client domain or direct database, filesystem, provider, or browser authority.

nodes.label: Workbench route state contains only low-sensitivity identifiers
nodes.rationale: URLs and history contain only low-sensitivity opaque view IDs and layout state; protected content and capabilities remain bounded in memory and are re-fetched under current authority.

nodes.label: New Assessment Wizard uses registered choices and resolved values
nodes.rationale: The wizard selects authorized registered repositories, catalog modes and profiles, and bounded targets and creates an exact versioned request rather than a browser-owned security configuration.

nodes.label: Start Preflight discloses the effective contract before confirmation
nodes.rationale: Before confirmation the service resolves and discloses the effective subject, policy, profile, composition, egress, protection, budget, gaps, and claim limits under one digest that the user may accept or cancel but not edit.

nodes.label: Assessment progress is a revision-bound phase and Coverage View
nodes.rationale: Assessment Detail derives phase, attempt, coverage, milestone, budget, blocker, and terminal facts from one labeled snapshot revision; wait signals only trigger refetch.

nodes.label: Role Cards show governed lineage not chat authority
nodes.rationale: Role cards expose governed definition, lineage, lifecycle, provider, budget, milestones, evidence, candidates, disposition, and challenges without implying conversational or approval authority.

nodes.label: Role Detail is immutable and cannot accept ad-hoc instructions
nodes.rationale: Role detail is an immutable authorized view; further analysis requires a reviewed service command and kernel-admitted durable attempt, never an unrecorded live instruction.

nodes.label: Deep independent passes remain hidden from peers until frozen
nodes.rationale: Peer outputs remain hidden until initial contributions freeze, and UI observation cannot feed live peers or collapse independent contributions into apparent consensus.

Available Actions Are Service-Projected, Not Client-Inferred
nodes.rationale: Keep action eligibility authoritative, revision-bound, and fail-safe instead of duplicating lifecycle rules in the client.

nodes.label: BLOCKED View Explains Recovery Without Offering a Bypass
nodes.rationale: Explain blockers and authorized recovery while withholding controls that could fabricate coverage, verdict, or completion.

nodes.label: Finding Triage View Keeps Domain Dimensions Separate
nodes.rationale: Preserve finding identity, validation, severity, policy, evidence, and coverage dimensions rather than collapsing them into one editable score.

nodes.label: Evidence View Starts Redacted and Reauthorizes Sensitive Content
nodes.rationale: Default to metadata and redacted summaries, requiring fresh purpose-specific authorization for bounded sensitive payload access.

nodes.label: Risk Decision Form Records a Governed Immutable Decision
nodes.rationale: Record risk through authoritative policy and identity checks, discard local sensitive input, and never claim optimistic acceptance.

nodes.label: Critical Break-Glass Requires Two Independent Operator Invocations
nodes.rationale: Require two independently authenticated matching attestations so browser state, impersonation fields, or repeated actions cannot satisfy dual authority.

nodes.label: Export UI Previews Profile and Destination While Service Performs Delivery
nodes.rationale: Let the browser preview authorized delivery but keep canonical construction, credentials, destination choice, writing, and receipts in the service.

nodes.label: Reconnect Recovers from ID, Revision, and Idempotency
nodes.rationale: Recover from service truth and original idempotency identities rather than treating browser cache or disconnect as authoritative continuation.

nodes.label: Browser Persistence Excludes Sensitive Assessment Payloads
nodes.rationale: Keep sensitive assessment, authority, repository, export, and evidence data out of durable browser storage and logs.

nodes.label: Workbench Inherits Host Web Security and Is Accessible and Bilingual
nodes.rationale: Honor host web controls while delivering accessible English and Simplified Chinese UI without leaking privileged capabilities.

nodes.label: Control Plane Integration Is an Optional By-Value Adapter
nodes.rationale: Integrate through public contracts, verified repository binding, package-owned authority, and sealed submissions by value without shared mutable internals.

nodes.label: Control Plane Cancellation Resolves Only an Existing Assessment
nodes.rationale: Ensure cancellation looks up stable prior work and never starts a new assessment or converts verification failure into success.

nodes.label: Cancellation Crash Checkpoint Preserves the Exact Assessment
nodes.rationale: Prove restart reconciliation returns the same canceled assessment without exposing or persisting the non-authorizing test checkpoint.

nodes.label: Control Plane External Failure Uses Provider-Neutral Constructor
nodes.rationale: Return bounded provider-neutral failure values without disclosing private security data or fabricating submissions and mission outcomes.

nodes.label: Control Plane Assurance Retry Starts a Distinct Assessment
nodes.rationale: Give successor invocations independent assessment identity while reserving recovery for the same durable invocation and revalidating reusable subject publications.

nodes.label: Control Plane Repository Binding Precedes Assessment Start
nodes.rationale: Create no assessment until host resolution and a process-local kernel assertion prove the configured and mission repositories share one canonical root.

nodes.label: Host Repository Provider Is a Trusted Composition Adapter
nodes.rationale: Register deployment-owned roots through package authority without exporting invocation minting or direct registry mutation.

nodes.label: Package-Private Protocol Symbols Have Versioned Process Identities
nodes.rationale: Keep compatible private same-process protocol keys stable across bundles without exposing authority or public exports.

nodes.label: Export Delivery Recovery Is Service-Owned and Bounded
nodes.rationale: Persist intent before I/O and make lifecycle-bound service retries bounded, idempotent, observable, and integrity checked.

nodes.label: Export Expiry Uses Two-Phase Exact-Target Reaping
nodes.rationale: Deny access before exact-file deletion, retain a durable tombstone, and reconcile interrupted reaping without recursive or caller-selected deletion.
